segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Well, I just wonder because we always have the Democrats on and they talk about what Trump's doing. We ask, you know, what are you doing to push back as a Democrat? Obviously, you're the minority. I thought it was interesting. You have a bill that is you're introducing that aims to put guardrails on donations to presidential libraries. I should note that I'm asking you about that as tonight the president is dining

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: With

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: the Qataris at the White House after, of course, they're giving him the plane.
I

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: wonder what your expectations are for that. So,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: look, we've had a problem before Donald Trump came along with presidents

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: taking donations to their presidential library while they're still sitting in office and while they can still offer pardons or cut tariff deals or approve mergers. It's just that Donald Trump
has

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: has now just put that on steroids with the $400

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: airplane, a $400 million airplane from the Qataris with the settlement

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: of the paramount bogus lawsuit. And who knows?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: How much other money is being funneled right now into a future

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: Trump library because there are no rules. There's no rules about having to disclose that money, no caps on disclosing it, and no limits on who can do it. Foreign governments, people seeking pardons, anybody can make these contributions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: So the bill that I introduced, and I've got a group of co-sponsors around this, including Senator Blumenthal here in the Senate. The bill that I've introduced just says, we've got to put some limits on this and say that while you're still president, you can't be out there soliciting or accepting funds

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_07
segments.text: from people for your future library. We've got to have just some sensible safeguards in place. And here's what's interesting.
A

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_07
segments.text: couple of years ago, the Republicans teamed up with Democrats, with Representative Moskowitz in the House, and they introduced the same bill. We never got it over here, never had a chance
to vote on it. But

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: this should be a bipartisan effort. It is not in anyone's interest to have a president of the United States even taking on the appearance
of

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: selling favors to foreign countries or selling favors

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: to people who want pardons. And so presidential libraries, let's cut that one off as one of the ways that Donald Trump can wallow in corruption. We'll

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: see. I think you might struggle to get some Republican Senate support, but we'll see if that happens.
